surprises.description: Smithfield lowered full-year adjusted operating profit guidance to $900 million-$1 billion, below the preview’s $1.025-$1.125 billion estimate and with the low end below the preview’s $1 billion danger threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management lowered total company full-year adjusted operating profit outlook to $900 million-$1 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate for the reset: ~$1,025–1,125M”; the preview also said “below $1,000M is a problem.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.26, below the preview’s $0.29 consensus and the preview’s view that the quarter was “more likely to clear than not.” The result was still at the low end of the preview’s own $0.26-$0.38 guidance-based bridge.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS: $0.29”; “The quarter is more likely to clear than not.”

surprises.description: Packaged Meats showed more margin resilience than the preview’s key downside debate contemplated: profit reached $230 million and margin expanded 80 basis points despite lower sales, rather than cracking under the pressure the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Packaged Meats delivered its second-highest Q3 operating profit on record, growing operating profit to $230 million with margin expanding 80 basis points to 11.6% despite a 5.2% sales decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bear case required “PM margin (13.1% in Q2) to crack under freight, fuel and packaging inflation” and identified PM profit of “~$230M” in its base case.

surprises.description: Packaged Meats outperformed the preview’s simple expectation that branded volume growth would hold: Smithfield grew volume while the industry contracted, gained share across its five largest categories, and its e-commerce growth also exceeded industry growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Smithfield was the only company in its competitive set to grow volume (~1% vs. industry -3.3%), gaining share in all five largest categories, while e-commerce volume grew 22.5% versus 13.4% industry growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “confirmation that branded volume growth held through a ‘cautious consumer’ quarter” and noted Q2 branded lunch meat volume growth of 9.5% and share gains in five large categories.

surprises.description: The completed Nathan’s Famous acquisition adds an immediate recurring EPS benefit from about $33 million per year in avoided license costs, a development the preview did not flag; the near-term Q4 contribution is limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed the Nathan's Famous acquisition, which is immediately accretive to adjusted EPS primarily by repatriating about $33 million per year in prior license costs, though Q4 contribution will be de minimis.”

surprises.description: A new long-term supply agreement will reduce internally produced hogs by roughly 900,000 annually and take the company below its 10 million hog target, a structural operating change not anticipated in the preview; the supplied facts do not quantify its earnings effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new long-term supply agreement with a joint venture partner will reduce internally produced hogs by roughly 900,000 per year, pushing the company below its 10 million hog target.”
